chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us, who said: He narrated to me from Abu Ishaq – meaning Ibrahim ibn Hashim – from Ibn Sinan and others from those he mentioned, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Qur'an and the Criterion: Are they two things or one thing?
He said: Then he said: The Qur'an is the entirety of the Book, and the Criterion is the clear part which is obligatory to act by.

key_terms.الْفُرْقَانِ: The Criterion, referring to the clear/decisive part
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: The Qur'an, referring here to the complete Book

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Qur'an and the Furqan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq distinguishing between the Qur'an as the comprehensive collection of revelation and the Furqan as the specific, decisive verses (*al-Muhkamat*) that serve as the primary basis for legal and practical action. This distinction highlights the Shia hermeneutical approach to understanding the Qur'an's layered nature, where the 'Criterion' functions not merely as a title but as the operational core of divine guidance. Such clarification aids in resolving apparent contradictions by prioritizing the clear, actionable texts over the more nuanced or allegorical ones.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad, that he said: I was told by Abu Ishaq – meaning Ibrahim bin Hashim – from Ibn Sinan and others from those he mentioned, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about the Qur’an and the Criterion: Are they two things or one thing?
He said: Then he said: The Qur’an is the complete Book, and the Criterion is the clear part of it which is obligatory to act by.
